nodes.author: prisma
nodes.rationale: Prisma blocks destructive commands (migrate reset, db push --force-reset, db push --accept-data-loss) when it detects an AI agent until the user gives explicit, non-inferred consent, because an agent could otherwise silently destroy database data.

nodes.label: antislop-copywriting Skill
nodes.rationale: Never invent facts (R-17/R-36/R-38); do not over-sterilize (R-37); voiceless copy is as machine-made as AI tells.

nodes.label: antislop-human Skill
nodes.rationale: Contrast, keyboard, focus, states, and mobile exclusions; accessibility is part of the core promise that the UI holds up (C-4).

nodes.label: antislop-layoutmobile Skill

nodes.label: antislop Core Filter

nodes.label: Border Glow Pattern

nodes.label: CSS Visuals Pattern
nodes.rationale: Product-accurate illustrations from HTML + tokens, zero assets; each maps to a product concept in a code comment (R-22).

nodes.label: Closing CTA Band Pattern
nodes.rationale: Bookend to hero: bottom-center glow mirrors hero top-left; single specific CTA; footer does not repeat it.

nodes.label: Hero Dashboard Card Pattern
nodes.rationale: The 3D card IS the product UI: real approval states make it the most honest hero visual; CSS perspective + JS tilt, no WebGL.

nodes.label: Highlights Strip Pattern
nodes.rationale: 3-4 real product facts replacing logo bars and invented stats; empty beats deceptive (R-17, R-38).

nodes.label: Pattern Library Index
nodes.rationale: Battle-tested, antislop-verified, WCAG-checked starting points; adapt, do not copy-paste.

nodes.label: Scroll Reveal Pattern
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency IntersectionObserver reveals; hero loads immediately, body at 12%; all prefers-reduced-motion guarded.

nodes.label: Storytelling Pairs Pattern
nodes.rationale: Alternating text+visual pairs replace 3-step lists; DOM text-first for screen readers, CSS order flips for RHYTHM 2.

nodes.label: Typography System Pattern
nodes.rationale: Token type scale, six hierarchy levels; eyebrow is a plain span not pill badge; wordmark brand-name-only with DESIGN.md reason.

nodes.label: antislop-ui Skill
nodes.rationale: UI/visual depth: color, layout, components, decoration, flow, motion; proven patterns in patterns/ are adapted, not copy-pasted.

nodes.label: Mobile Reflow Principle
nodes.rationale: Mobile layout is a different layout, not desktop at a smaller size; it must re-stack, rescale, and re-order with intent.

nodes.label: Core Principle (Purpose Test)
nodes.rationale: Rejects technique without purpose, not technique itself; done means purpose test passes, identity exists, and it works.

nodes.label: Craftsmanship Standard (C-1..C-5)
nodes.rationale: Not-slop is the floor; five criteria: Intentionality, Functional Completeness, Content-Driven Composition, Resilience, Evidence Over Claims.

nodes.label: Delivery Gate (Mandatory)
nodes.rationale: PASS/FAIL report with concrete evidence before delivering; cannot be delegated; a FAIL must never ship.

nodes.label: Design Read
nodes.rationale: One-line declaration inferring dials from direction, one decisive question when ambiguous, or draft-without-direction at 1/1/1.

nodes.label: First-Run Install Wizard
nodes.rationale: Offer-not-require skill install; agent never downloads SKILL.md files from network (would fetch its own next prompt).

nodes.label: Hard Gate Rules (Absolute)
nodes.rationale: Protect honesty, function, and accessibility; any Hard Gate break is a FAIL regardless of purpose.

nodes.label: Liveliness Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Removing slop leaves a void; liveliness must be added deliberately via dials and levers, not bans.

nodes.label: Antislop Pointer Block (Entry File)
nodes.rationale: Marker block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md routing to core plus installed skills; source of truth for installed skills.

nodes.label: Purpose-Gate Rules
nodes.rationale: Technique allowed when hierarchy/identity purpose is stated and written down; fails only as default without purpose.

nodes.label: Quality Locks (Consistency)
nodes.rationale: Consistency requirements; R-05 keyed to RHYTHM dial, R-31 upgraded to keystone.

nodes.label: R-01: Color & Gradients
nodes.rationale: Default gradient family forbidden without purpose; allowed for brand identity or stated hierarchy with reason written.

nodes.label: R-02: Em Dash Ban
nodes.rationale: Em dash is a reliable AI tell; banned in agent-authored text with documentation carve-outs and R-37 voice-sample protocol.

nodes.label: R-03: Mobile Responsiveness
nodes.rationale: Mobile layout perfect not afterthought; no overflow/clipping; 44px tap targets; consistent spacing across breakpoints.

nodes.label: R-05: Layout & Page Structure
nodes.rationale: Forbids AI template layouts; structure from content needs and RHYTHM dial, not training-data default order.

nodes.label: R-06: Typography
nodes.rationale: Typeface from brand character, not model default roster; monospace aesthetic and wide-tracked uppercase need written reasons.

nodes.label: R-09: Badges
nodes.rationale: Capsule AI badges forbidden as default; only when functionally needed with reason; no full decoration stack.

nodes.label: R-13: Glow Dose Cap
nodes.rationale: Glow amplifies attention; everywhere amplifies nothing. Max 1-2 focus accents; forbidden across all surfaces at once.

nodes.label: R-17: Data & Numbers
nodes.rationale: Statistics without a real source forbidden; empty is better than deceptive.

nodes.label: R-19: Animations
nodes.rationale: Motion needs written UX purpose and MOTION dial match; no template stacks or endless loops; prefers-reduced-motion required.

nodes.label: R-22: Illustrations
nodes.rationale: Generic illustrations forbidden without written product connection; real screenshots or none otherwise.

nodes.label: R-25: Color Contrast
nodes.rationale: WCAG AA required (4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large); contrast is local, test the whole text area not one point.

nodes.label: R-31: Every Decision Needs a Reason
nodes.norm_label: r-31: every decision needs a reason
nodes.rationale: Keystone: one-line reason for every major decision; writing the reason forces intent and underpins the Purpose-Gate.

nodes.label: R-32: Keyboard Accessibility
nodes.rationale: Keyboard reachable/operable with visible focus; outline:none without replacement forbidden; mouse-only UI unfinished.

nodes.label: R-35: Verify Before You Deliver
nodes.rationale: Never-run design is unfinished; click every interactive element and report element-by-element evidence.

nodes.label: R-36: No Fabricated Claims
nodes.rationale: Invented security, compliance, performance, testimonial, or statistic claims forbidden; no real data means no claim.

nodes.label: R-37: Design Direction Required
nodes.rationale: Load DESIGN.md or brand guidance first; no direction means labeled draft at dials 1/1/1, never a silent sterile default.

nodes.label: R-38: Real Content or Honest Placeholder
nodes.norm_label: r-38: real content or honest placeholder
nodes.rationale: Real information or explicitly labeled placeholder only; empty section beats fabricated one.

nodes.label: Three Dials (ENERGY/RHYTHM/MOTION)
nodes.rationale: Three levels not ten: uniform-vs-varied is binary and checkable; continuous 6-vs-7 is not enforceable.

nodes.label: Two Usage Modes (During/After)
nodes.rationale: Ask whether to apply during work or audit after; both keep direction (R-37), asset-ask (R-23), Delivery Gate.

nodes.label: Gate Ring Visual
nodes.rationale: Maps to human approval gate; layered box-shadow glow without pulsing animation (MOTION 1).

nodes.label: Platform Status Grid Visual
nodes.rationale: Maps to multi-platform publishing; state-coded borders communicate build progress without invented metrics.

nodes.label: Stacked Idea Cards Visual
nodes.rationale: Maps to AI generating multiple outputs; stacked rotated cards read as multiple things at once.

nodes.label: Glow Budget (R-13)
nodes.rationale: Two ambient glows max (hero top-left + CTA bottom-center bookend) plus one interactive border glow counted separately.

nodes.label: Motion Inventory
nodes.rationale: All motion prefers-reduced-motion guarded; each animation serves a distinct purpose, not decoration.

nodes.label: Premium Landing Structure
nodes.rationale: Proven order: hero split, storytelling pairs, highlights strip, arch/security/roadmap, CTA band, footer; conversion-focused without template defaults.

nodes.label: Dark Mode WCAG Contrast Reference
nodes.rationale: Computed dark-palette pairings; obvious muted #637669 fails 4.06:1 on #070c09 so test against deepest bg.

nodes.label: UI Skill Checklist
nodes.rationale: UI-specific supplement run alongside the core Delivery Gate across color, type, layout, motion, dashboard, a11y.

nodes.label: Muted Text on Deep Backgrounds
nodes.rationale: Muted colors passing on medium-dark can fail on deeper brand bg; test against the deepest background, not the average dark.

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: No draft can be published without explicit human approval. Highest-criticality provision: it enforces the DRY_RUN=true safety default and prevents unreviewed AI-generated content from going live.

nodes.label: Moderation Policy Enforcement Before Approval
nodes.rationale: BrandProfile guardrails (tone, banned words, platform rules, compliance constraints) are enforced by ModerationService before any draft enters the approval gate, so violations are caught before human review rather than after publication.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative DRY_RUN Toggle
nodes.rationale: The DRY_RUN switch is persisted server-side in SystemState.settings and guarded by a confirmation dialog because disabling simulation mode silently allows real publishing; a client-only toggle would be unenforceable.

nodes.label: Phase 2 Tier 0/1/2 Prioritization
nodes.rationale: Plans are ranked by dependency order rather than plan size: Tier 0 (accounts, audit-log writers, automation, approval-gate hardening) blocks Phase 2 because the integration contract requires OAuth, audit evidence, durable queue dispatch, and a safe publish gate before any new adapter ships.

nodes.label: Collection Storage Name Addressing
nodes.rationale: Most common porting mistake: v6 model names address the client (prisma.user), but Next Mongo ORM keys are collection storage names — the @@map name or lowercased model name (db.orm.users).

nodes.label: MongoDB 8.0+ Server Floor
nodes.rationale: Prisma Next's Mongo target requires MongoDB 8.0+ and mongodb@^7 peer dependency, while v6 tolerated older servers — check the server version before planning a migration.

nodes.label: v6 MongoDB to Prisma Next Contract Mapping
nodes.norm_label: v6 mongodb to prisma next contract mapping
nodes.rationale: Prisma Next does not consume v6 schema.prisma as-is; translating mechanically without the mapping produces contracts that fail verification or silently change collection addressing.

nodes.label: Staged Read-Only Soak
nodes.rationale: Run the Next stack read-only against staging/production data alongside v6 and compare outputs before allowing writes; keep v6 runnable as the rollback path since rolling back is only a code rollback.

nodes.label: Direct vs Serverless Adapter Choice
nodes.rationale: Standard Node.js apps prefer @prisma/adapter-pg with a direct TCP URL (sslmode=require); edge/serverless runtimes use @prisma/adapter-ppg with @prisma/ppg only when the serverless driver is specifically needed.

nodes.label: create-db Instant Provisioning
nodes.rationale: Fastest way to a working Prisma Postgres for development, demos, and CI previews; databases are temporary by default, auto-deleted after ~24 hours unless claimed via the CLAIM_URL.

nodes.label: Management API OAuth 2.0 Flow
nodes.rationale: Best for acting on behalf of users across workspaces: authorize at auth.prisma.io/authorize, exchange the code at auth.prisma.io/token, then use the access token.

nodes.label: Workspace-Project-Branch-Database Resource Model
nodes.rationale: Branches are first-class resources: databases attach to a Branch, and branch-scoped env/databases are how preview isolation works.

nodes.label: Management API SDK
nodes.rationale: Typed endpoint methods remove auth and refresh boilerplate, reducing errors in production provisioning flows; Platform API evolves independently from Prisma ORM, so inspect the installed package's api.d.ts.

nodes.label: Management API Service Token Flow
nodes.rationale: Best for server-to-server operations in your own workspace: create the token in Console workspace settings, then send Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN on every request.

nodes.label: Workspace-Scoped Service Tokens
nodes.rationale: Service tokens authenticate server-to-server requests, are workspace-scoped (no project-scoped tokens), and must be stored in env vars or secret managers — never source code.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 Client Instantiation with Driver Adapter
nodes.norm_label: prisma 7 client instantiation with driver adapter
nodes.rationale: At runtime the adapter is mandatory: new PrismaClient() throws, datasourceUrl does not exist in Prisma 7, the import must be ./generated/prisma/client.js, and package.json needs type: module (ESM).

nodes.label: Accelerate URL Handling in v7
nodes.rationale: Driver adapters fail with prisma:// and prisma+postgres:// URLs; Accelerate users keep the URL and instantiate with accelerateUrl plus @prisma/extension-accelerate instead of an adapter.

nodes.label: Driver Adapter Requirement for SQL in v7
nodes.norm_label: driver adapter requirement for sql in v7
nodes.rationale: v7 requires driver adapters for SQL: no native engine binary in the Prisma Client SQL path, smaller bundles, better serverless/edge compatibility, native Node.js drivers, and explicit pool control.

nodes.label: Explicit Environment Loading with dotenv
nodes.rationale: v7 no longer auto-loads .env — import 'dotenv/config' first in prisma.config.ts (Bun loads .env automatically); several PRISMA_* engine and generate env vars are removed.

nodes.label: ESM-First Module System with CommonJS Fallback
nodes.norm_label: esm-first module system with commonjs fallback
nodes.rationale: v7 is ESM-first; CommonJS projects keep their setup and set moduleFormat = "cjs" in the generator instead of forcing ESM — module, moduleResolution, and moduleFormat must agree.

nodes.label: prisma.config.ts Central Configuration
nodes.rationale: Central CLI config at project root holding schema path, migrations, and datasource URLs moved out of schema.prisma; env() gives type safety but does NOT load .env files automatically.

nodes.label: Client Extensions Replace $use Middleware
nodes.rationale: The $extends({ query: { $allModels: { $allOperations } } }) pattern replaces middleware for timing, logging, and soft-delete interception in v7.

nodes.label: Removed Features in Prisma v7
nodes.rationale: Client middleware ($use), metrics preview, --skip-generate/--skip-seed flags, auto-generate/auto-seed behaviors, Prisma.validator, and rejectOnNotFound are removed — replaced by Client Extensions, driver-level metrics, explicit generate/seed, and satisfies.

nodes.label: prisma-client Generator Migration
nodes.rationale: prisma-client becomes the default generator: output path is required (no more node_modules generation), entrypoints split into client/browser/models/enums, engineType = "client", and Prisma.validator is replaced by TypeScript satisfies.

nodes.label: v6 to Prisma Next Cutover Verification Checklist
nodes.norm_label: v6 to prisma next cutover verification checklist
nodes.rationale: A v6 to Next migration is a client and workflow migration against the same MongoDB database — no data export/import; introducing one turns a code migration into an outage. The checklist keeps cutover observable and reversible.

nodes.label: Prisma Console and Local Studio Workflow
nodes.norm_label: prisma console and local studio workflow
nodes.rationale: Many Prisma Postgres tasks (Studio data inspection, metrics, connection details) are quickest in the Console, avoiding unnecessary API or CLI work.

nodes.label: Management API Programmatic Provisioning
nodes.rationale: The Management API is the source of truth for backend automation, multi-tenant onboarding, and controlled resource provisioning — more reliable than interactive workflows; mutation responses may reveal secrets once, so treat entire responses as secret until redacted.

nodes.label: Prisma Management API Conventions
nodes.rationale: Shared conventions (base URL, data envelope, ID prefixes, cursor pagination, error shapes) across all three prisma-postgres-* skills.

nodes.label: Craftsmanship Standard (C-1..C-5)
nodes.rationale: Five preference-agnostic criteria (intentionality, functional completeness, content-driven composition, resilience, evidence over claims) that make design done, not merely not-slop.

nodes.label: Delivery Gate
nodes.rationale: Mandatory PASS/FAIL report before delivery; a deliverable without a clean gate is unfinished and cannot be delegated to another workflow's summary.

nodes.label: Hard Gate Rule Group (R-02..R-38)
nodes.rationale: Absolute rules protecting honesty, function, and accessibility; breaking any is a FAIL regardless of purpose.

nodes.label: Liveliness Toolkit
nodes.rationale: Removing slop leaves a void; positive levers (focal point, hierarchical contrast, whitespace, deliberate accent, identity motif) must deliberately add energy.

nodes.label: Three Dials (ENERGY/RHYTHM/MOTION)
nodes.rationale: Three discrete levels make liveliness enforceable and checkable, unlike continuous 1-10 scales a reviewer cannot judge reliably.

nodes.label: Design Dials (ENERGY/RHYTHM/MOTION)
nodes.rationale: ENERGY 3 / RHYTHM 2 / MOTION 1 declared to keep high-energy bold structure with purposeful-only motion, per antislop dial mechanics.

nodes.label: Purpose-Gate Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Visual techniques (gradients, glow, icons, badges) are allowed only when a written purpose ties them to hierarchy or identity; the technique is not the problem, the purpose is.

nodes.label: R-31 Every Decision Must Have a Reason
nodes.norm_label: r-31 every decision must have a reason
nodes.rationale: Keystone rule: writing a one-line reason for every major visual decision forces intent, which is exactly what the Purpose-Gate checks.

nodes.label: Redis Durable Publish Queue
nodes.rationale: REDIS_URL backs durable publish queue and distributed rate limiting required for production security.

nodes.label: DB-backed SystemState Dry-Run Toggle
nodes.rationale: Dry-run/safety state moved from a module-level let to a singleton DB row because stateless runtimes do not guarantee memory persistence between invocations; this toggle gates simulated vs live posting.

nodes.label: Recommended v3 Information Architecture
nodes.rationale: Navigation follows user jobs (Content, Engagement, Analytics, Accounts) rather than implementation domains (Architecture Graph, WASM, CRM); System Diagnostics stays developer-only.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative Publishing
nodes.rationale: Publishing must be a server-side operation returning durable external job/result state; local client-side status flips are unsafe P0 defects.

nodes.label: No Widgets Until IA and Data Contracts Defined
nodes.norm_label: no widgets until ia and data contracts defined
nodes.rationale: The most important v3 decision: adding dashboard widgets before core SMM information architecture and data contracts exist multiplies rework on a prototype missing calendars, accounts, inbox, and real publishing.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative System Controls
nodes.rationale: Local React state for dryRun/wasmRanking lets the UI claim live publishing changed without backend change; every mutating control must call a server API and return persisted state.

nodes.label: DRY_RUN Safe Default
nodes.rationale: Live publishing is never enabled by default; DRY_RUN=true protects against accidental real posts without explicit approval.

nodes.label: Meta-first MVP Strategy
nodes.rationale: Planner stays network-agnostic; platform-specific behavior lives behind adapters so Meta/Instagram/Facebook can ship first without coupling the core pipeline.

nodes.label: Human Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Core product safety mechanism: no content reaches a live platform without explicit human approve/reject.

nodes.label: SMM Automation Platform
nodes.rationale: AI-assisted social media management platform whose defining property is human approval gates before any live publish.

nodes.label: R-37 Design Direction Required
nodes.rationale: Building UI without DESIGN.md or owner direction silently falls into sterile defaults; output must be labeled a draft with honest ENERGY 1/RHYTHM 1/MOTION 1 dials.

nodes.label: Approval Gate Identity Motif
nodes.rationale: The approval gate (step 04) gets a distinct visual because it is the product's core value proposition.

nodes.label: WASM-Python Output Equivalence Testing
nodes.rationale: WASM output must match Python exactly across 100+ cases with a feature-flag fallback, because divergence is the top migration risk.

nodes.label: JSX Syntax in Plain HTML Regression
nodes.norm_label: jsx syntax in plain html regression
nodes.rationale: className/onClick/style={{}} are not browser features in a static HTML file; they left the theme toggle inert and threw TypeError on every login.html load.

nodes.label: Missing CSS Brace Regression
nodes.rationale: One missing '}' in .sr-only made CSS error recovery swallow ~22k characters, dropping ~95% of the site stylesheet; verified with tinycss2 rather than guessed.

nodes.label: Workspace to Client Domain Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Agency/multi-client operation must be a first-class hierarchy (Workspace, Client, Brand, Social accounts, Campaigns, Content) rather than a placeholder dashboard section.

nodes.label: antislop Core Rule Set
nodes.rationale: A filter, not a style guide: rejects technique-without-purpose and requires liveliness so AI UI feels crafted rather than generic.

nodes.label: CRM Plan v2
nodes.rationale: Sequences Inbox/Contacts/Pipeline/Leads/Marketing by dependency and actual size rather than treating them as five equal tasks.

nodes.label: SMMAI Brand Direction
nodes.rationale: Source of truth for all visual decisions; written from user answers plus Zyno inspiration so antislop agents have direction before any UI change.

nodes.label: SiteNav Component Upgrade Plan
nodes.rationale: SiteNav is a fixed 64px glassmorphic header requiring scroll-spy, responsive mobile menu, shared ThemeProvider context, and WCAG AA focus states

nodes.label: Frontend Fix Plan v1 (Static Site Audit)
nodes.norm_label: frontend fix plan v1 (static site audit)

nodes.label: Frontend Fix Plan v2
nodes.rationale: Re-audit after v1 fixes introduced three new regressions more severe than the originals; documents what changed while v1 remains the backlog.

nodes.label: SMMAI Plan v3 Dashboard Architecture Review
nodes.norm_label: smmai plan v3 dashboard architecture review
nodes.rationale: Supersedes dashboard assumptions in v1/v2; inventories the prototype, separates essential vs optional components, and defines the production SMM information architecture.

nodes.label: SMM Pipeline Architecture Flow
nodes.rationale: Draft generation must flow through moderation, human approval, dry-run-default publishing, then analytics feedback so the graph reflects end-to-end pipeline state; each stage is a deliberate safety or quality checkpoint.

nodes.label: Git Safety Rules (Non-Negotiable)
nodes.rationale: Destructive git commands previously destroyed work on this account; rules forbid clean/reset/checkout abuse, secret commits, and pushing to main to protect the repo.

nodes.label: Emerald-on-Deep-Black Palette
nodes.rationale: Emerald on deep green-cast black creates Zyno-level contrast punch; the green cast is the brand differentiator, avoiding generic blue-midnight SaaS and purple AI-cliche palettes.

nodes.label: Waspy Hybrid WASM Migration Strategy
nodes.rationale: Migrate only pure-compute hot paths via Waspy (Rust AOT, 0.2-6KB binaries, 2-5x CPython speed) for best ROI with minimal risk; alternatives embed runtimes and bloat binaries.

nodes.label: Visual System Conflict Resolution
nodes.rationale: Do not import the analytics-dashboard skill's Inter/orange tokens; use its component architecture only, mapped onto canonical SMMAI design tokens so one product has one visual language.

nodes.label: Task 1.1 Pin Prisma CLI to Stable
nodes.norm_label: task 1.1 pin prisma cli to stable

nodes.label: Prisma CLI Stable Pin (7.10.0)
nodes.rationale: prisma CLI was pinned to 7.10.0 to match @prisma/client; the 8.0.0-rc.17 pre-release lacks a generate command.

nodes.label: Prisma Neon Driver Adapter
nodes.rationale: Function-per-request runtimes exhaust TCP connection limits under load if each invocation opens a plain connection; the adapter is a correctness fix, not platform-specific.

nodes.label: toClientDTO Response Shaping
nodes.rationale: Maps flat Prisma postCount/lastPostAt columns into the nested posts shape ClientsTable already expects instead of changing every consumer.

nodes.label: Database Enum/Shape as Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: database enum/shape as source of truth
nodes.rationale: The DB shape wins casing/shape disagreements between UI and schema (with a documented exception when the UI has far more working call sites); picking this once prevents trial-and-error rediscovery.

nodes.label: Vercel Deployment Root and Package-Manager Runbook
nodes.norm_label: vercel deployment root and package-manager runbook

nodes.label: R-13 Glow Dose Cap
nodes.rationale: Glow is a focus accent on at most 1-2 elements; simultaneous glow on cards, buttons, badges, icons, backgrounds, and borders is forbidden.

nodes.label: R-13 Glow Dose Cap (Brand Instance)
nodes.rationale: Only two glow elements allowed total (hero ambient + arch border glow) to satisfy antislop R-13 while keeping the Zyno-inspired depth.

nodes.label: Login Page Theme Toggle
nodes.rationale: localStorage-persisted light/dark toggle satisfying DESIGN.md R-21 and antislop R-34 so both WCAG-verified modes work across pages.

nodes.label: R-34 Every Theme You Ship Must Work
nodes.norm_label: r-34 every theme you ship must work
nodes.rationale: A shipped theme toggle must be fully functional in both modes; a dark mode that breaks light mode is a defect.

nodes.label: Inbox Gated on Platform Adapters
nodes.rationale: Inbox needs real platform API connections; a mocked inbox with no data source looks done and is worse than not building it, so it is sequenced after Pipeline/Leads.

nodes.label: Next.js Breaking Changes Agent Warning
nodes.rationale: This Next.js version has breaking changes that may differ from training data — read node_modules/next/dist/docs before writing code; the warning block is re-added by next dev, so commit it with your work.

nodes.label: Plus Jakarta Sans Typography
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Inter (the AI default) for rounder terminals and a more human, warm-geometric professional feel.

nodes.label: Agent Safety Consent for Destructive Commands
nodes.norm_label: agent safety consent for destructive commands

nodes.label: One-Time Service Token Value Disclosure
nodes.rationale: A newly created token's data.value is returned exactly once; transfer it directly to the intended secret store without logging the response — later list calls return only metadata and valueHint.

nodes.label: Management API Resource ID Prefixes
nodes.rationale: Every resource ID carries a type prefix (proj_, db_, con_, wksp_); omitting the prefix causes resource-not-found (404) errors on API requests.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.0 User-Scoped Access
nodes.rationale: OAuth is used when acting on behalf of a user (partner/integrator flows); service tokens are the recommended method for standard database setup.

nodes.label: Direct Connection String Endpoint
nodes.rationale: Use data.database.connections[0].endpoints.direct.connectionString as DATABASE_URL; ignore pooled and accelerate endpoints for new projects — direct is all you need.

nodes.label: Driver Adapter Package Matrix
nodes.rationale: Maps each database to its adapter package and underlying driver (e.g., PostgreSQL → @prisma/adapter-pg over pg; Prisma Postgres serverless → @prisma/adapter-ppg over @prisma/ppg).

nodes.label: New Text Document (Empty)
nodes.rationale: Empty placeholder text file tracked in repository root
